text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
SUGAR - SUGAR: World market for March 17, 1997

White sugar futures in London closed lower after an uninspiring session. London's spot May contract lost $0.40 to close at $307.00 per tonne, while August gave up $0.40 to close at $305.70 per tonne. There was some light activity on the nearby May/May arbitrage but interest was thin. Raw sugar futures in New York closed slightly higher across the board with front month May adding 2 points to close at 10.92 cents/lb, while July closed 4 points higher at 10.67 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 2 and 4 points. There was no fresh news to influence prices.

AUSTRALIA - Australian raw sugar production is forecast to rise to 5.45 million tonnes 94 net titre in 1997/98 (July/June) from 5.32 million in 1996/97, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said. It forecast 1997/98 sugar exports would rise to 4.60 million tonnes worth an estimated A$1.47 bn, from 4.25 million worth A$1.42 bn in 1996/97. Turning to the world market, ABARE said world raw sugar prices are forecast to fall to an average 10.3 cents/lb in 1997/98, from 10.8 cents/lb in 1996/97. It added that after falling to 123 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, from 126 million in 1995/96, world sugar production is forecast to rise slightly to 124 million tonnes in 1997/98, mainly because of increased output in Latin America and India. However, trade sources in India expect production to fall by one million tonnes in 1997/98.

BRAZIL - Weather conditions in the Center South continue to be favourable with the state of Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais, Goias, Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul reporting isolated rain showers and good sunshine. Producers expect cane output in 1997/98 to be up on last year because of good water reserves in the soil, higher temperatures, which are almost ideal for boosting cane growth, good sunshine and passing showers, particularly in the evening hours.

SINGAPORE - Sugar imports in October 1996 amounted to 28,223 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 26,760 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1996 (January/October) up to 254,051 tonnes against 230,149 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 271,334 tonnes, somewhat below the record high of 1994 of 285,420 tonnes. Major countries of origin in January/October 1996 were Australia with 60,001 tonnes raws against 154,014 tonnes, Thailand with 80,000 tonnes raws against 8,000 tonnes and Fiji with 20,000 tonnes compared to nil.

The largest suppliers of white sugar in 1996 were Malaysia with 55,228 tonnes against 40,767 tonnes and Australia with 12,083 tonnes compared to 2,393 tonnes. Sugar exports in January/October 1996 amounted to 9,137 tonnes compared to 17,304 tonnes. Total exports in calendar year 1995 amounted to 22,136 tonnes compared to 23,391 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of destination in January/October 1996 were Brunei with 1,875 tonnes whites against 1,444 tonnes and the Philippines with 1,507 tonnes compared to 6,752 tonnes.

Bangladesh state-owned Sugar and Food Corporation has bought 25,000 tonnes of white sugar at $347.47 c&f per tonne for shipment by 1st May. Moreover, the corporation has called for bids for a total of 50,000 tonnes of sugar for shipment by June 9.
